description: The Storm Events Database of NOAA's National Centers for Environmental Information records high-intensity storms, rare or unusual weather phenomena and other significant weather events in the United States, compiled from National Weather Service Storm Data reports. Each event record gives begin and end date, time and location (state, county or zone, latitude and longitude), event type, direct and indirect injuries and deaths, property and crop damage estimates, magnitude, flood cause, tornado F or EF scale, length and width, and episode and event narratives, with separate fatality and location files. Coverage starts in 1950; the bulk files run by year from 1950 to 2026, and NCEI states that early years hold only tornadoes, later years also hail and thunderstorm wind, and all 48 event types from 1996. The files are refreshed regularly (the 2026 file was dated 18 September 2026). Data are accessible online at no cost through the search interface and as gzip-compressed CSV files over HTTPS, as a US federal product. Caveats: damage figures are estimates reported by forecast offices, event type coverage changes over time, and early records are incomplete. It supports historical event analysis and hazard exposure of power, transport and water infrastructure to floods, storms, heat, cold and wildfire; related records are the NCEI global historical hazards, IBTrACS and EM-DAT.
